currentAndFutureRenderBehavior.todayNull: baked.provenance.landUseSource is null for a no-land-use parcel. The construction is `baked.provenance.landUseSource ? [{label:'Land-use source', detail: baked.provenance.landUseSource}] : []` -- null is falsy, so NO entry is added for 'Land-use source' at all. Nothing renders for it, in either the collapsed or expanded Sources disclosure. This is the 'harmless' behavior the dispatch refers to.
currentAndFutureRenderBehavior.afterUpstreamFixObject: Once landUseSource becomes `{verdict, scope, asOf, basis}` (or similar), that object is TRUTHY, so the ternary DOES add the entry: `{label:'Land-use source', detail: <object>}`. `entries` is a plain JS array built eagerly on every render regardless of whether the disclosure is open. If a customer then taps 'Sources' (isOpen becomes true), SourcesDisclosure maps over entries and renders `{e.detail}` as a JSX child.
currentAndFutureRenderBehavior.empiricalCorrectionToTheDispatchWording: Verified live (renderToStaticMarkup, react-dom 18.3.1, this repo's real SourcesDisclosure component) with entries=[{label:'Land-use source', detail:{verdict:'absent-verified',scope:'county',asOf:'2026-09-08',basis:'no coded land-use record'}}], isOpen=true: this does NOT silently render the text " . [object Object]" -- it THROWS 'Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {verdict, scope, asOf, basis})'. React explicitly validates JSX children and rejects plain objects; it does not implicitly toString() them the way template-literal interpolation would. The one place in this file that IS a literal template literal touching this value is the React `key` prop one line below (`key={`${e.label}-${e.detail}`}`), which WOULD silently coerce to the string '[object Object]' via toString() -- but `key` is stripped by React before reaching the DOM, so that particular coercion is never customer-visible. The dispatch's underlying claim (a customer-facing break for every null-land-use parcel) is TRUE and confirmed; the specific literal string it quotes is not what actually happens -- the real failure mode is a harder one (a React render crash inside the disclosure's expanded state, not a garbled-but-visible text node).
